title: Choose the visual world (re-roll 2, plain register)
question: The dice's pick plus the two strongest dealt challengers, spread subtler / same / pushed further; the owner's two keepers stay on the table.
channel: Crush question form with pictures (owner's standing preference: look choices in the form, no pop-up pages)
ownerWords: I like Design Manual and Research paper, but I want to see trhee more - but don't discard these. Make sure you are using the dice from $impeccable / Give me one subtler, one about same level, and one pushed further
kept: The general design (three columns: chat list with branch tree, conversation, visuals panel with the limits row) stays; the world changes.
candidates: Seven fresh grounded candidates written before the roll, in ~/.cache/crush-gui-briefs/look-candidates.md: 1 O'Reilly animal books, 2 Dieter Rams / Braun, 3 Chess analysis books, 4 Isotype, 5 Shooting script with revision colours, 6 Swiss topographic map, 7 LEGO building instructions.
pickCard: Omitted: optional, and the owner asked for three options from the dice.

bar.note: As tidy as Zed (aligned grid, even spacing, a real type scale), with a little more dazzle than Zed has.

options.label: Chess Book
options.lineage: chess analysis books (Chess Informant, figurine notation)
options.thesis: Crush set like a chess analysis book: a chat is the main line and every branch a variation hanging off it.
options.viewport: Standard three columns, nearly monochrome. The main chat bold in the chat list with its branches indented beneath as bracketed side lines; the selected chat inverted, white on black; one deep red only on things you can press.
options.signature: Branches as variations off the main line.

raised.raise: Selection is a full inversion (white on black), never a tinted row.
The one saturated colour appears only on things you can press.
A chat whose state changed keeps its mark until you open it.
Every visual names the message it came from, like an atlas index pointing into its plate.

options.risk: Very plain; it can read as a normal app with little of the world showing.
options.redraw: First draw dropped the signature (standard tree lines, no variation notation), so the world showed only as a colour scheme; prompt made the bracketed italic side lines explicit and redrew once.

options.label: Scholar's Edition
options.lineage: reference-setting editions drawn by a ruling engine
options.thesis: Crush set like a fine reference edition: bone paper, hairline ruling, and a vermilion rail of keys marking where each chat branches.
options.viewport: Standard three columns on bone paper; a thin vermilion rail down the conversation's left edge carries lettered keys at branch points and tool runs.
options.case: Beats the roll on audience identification (the owner reads papers and kept the Research paper style); ties on product clarity.
options.risk: Light theme, and close in feeling to the Research paper keeper.

options.label: Airport Signs
options.thesis: Crush signed like an airport: yellow means wayfinding and nothing else, and every branch is a signed junction.
options.viewport: Standard three columns: the chat list a signal-yellow panel (selected chat a black band), conversation and right panel sign-black; branches signed with arrow squares; usage numbers big like gate numbers.
options.case: Beats the roll on product clarity (one message per band, only the choices ahead); ties on audience identification.
options.risk: Loud; a large yellow area can tire the eyes in long sessions, and the warning colour must stay clearly apart from the yellow.

options.label: Datamatics
options.case: Loses both axes: pure black and white with monospace everywhere drops AI identity and warning colour, and on a working chat screen it slides toward the terminal costume the brief rules out.

options.label: Warm Consumer App
options.case: Loses both axes, and its soft-cornered cards break the owner's ban on everything in rounded cards.
options.kept: One saturated colour only where something can be pressed.

options.label: Boarding Pass and Gate Board
options.case: Loses both axes: the owner already passed on travel ephemera (the jet-age ticket), and its clarity only ties.
options.kept: A changed row stays marked until you have seen it.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.case: Loses both axes: weak tie to the owner's world, and navy with amber sits close to the look the owner called generic.
options.kept: Every visual points back to its source, like an atlas index.

buildPath.note: The brief pins the mockup-led workflow; a pinned decision beats the roll's code-led default for operate surfaces.

canonCard.label: Keep the current look
canonCard.thesis: The category standard, played straight: charcoal and amber, as in style-2, held to Zed's finish.
canonCard.risk: What most AI chat apps look like.
